Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the NovaTech Semiconductor Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today's call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Davies, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and welcome to NovaTech Semiconductor’s Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Robert Miller, CEO; Susan Chen, CFO; and David Lee, Chief Technology Officer.
Earlier today, we published our earnings press release and slides, which are available on our IR site. Please note this call may contain forward-looking statements. Now, I’ll turn it over to Robert Miller.

Robert Miller, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet. Hello, everyone.

Let’s start with a look at the quarter:

This quarter, we achieved significant progress, including a robust 39.1% operating margin, translating to an operating income of NT$28.1 billion. This performance reflects our strategic pricing initiatives, operational efficiency improvements, and favorable market conditions. For the first half of the year, our operating margin stands at a healthy 37.3%.

We’re seeing strong performance in our wafer sales, where we shipped a total of 17.5 million wafers, representing a 4.3% increase compared to the previous quarter. This growth is particularly encouraging considering the ongoing macroeconomic headwinds.

These results reflect our strategy in action. I’ll now hand it over to Susan Chen to discuss the financials.

Susan Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Robert, and hello, everyone.

Let’s take a closer look at the numbers:

As Robert mentioned, we shipped a total of 17.5 million wafers this quarter, a 4.3% increase from the 16.8 million in Q1. 300mm wafers accounted for approximately 65% of total wafer shipments, increasing by 5.1%, driven by memory and leading-edge logic applications. 200mm wafers saw a more modest 2.8% increase, driven by analog, power management, and discrete devices, particularly in the automotive and industrial sectors. Smaller wafers experienced a slight contraction of 1.2%. Our overall wafer ASP increased by 2.7% this quarter compared to the previous quarter, thanks to a higher proportion of 300mm wafers, pricing discipline, and a favorable foreign exchange impact, which contributed roughly 0.8 percentage points to the ASP increase.

Our Q2 operating margin reached a robust 39.1%, translating to an operating income of NT$28.1 billion. This is a 2.7 percentage point improvement compared to Q1, driven by several factors. Our "Project Phoenix" initiative, aimed at streamlining our global logistics network, yielded a 12% reduction in transportation costs, or approximately NT$800 million in cost savings. We also saw a shift in product mix towards higher-margin offerings, particularly within our enterprise solutions segment, with the successful launch of our "Titan" server line, targeted at AI and machine learning applications, seeing a 25% increase in sales volume compared to Q1. Marketing expenses were strategically reduced by 8% compared to Q1, reflecting the seasonality of our campaigns. Furthermore, favorable currency fluctuations contributed roughly 0.3 percentage points to the operating margin improvement. Compared to Q2 2023, when the operating margin was 33.5%, the current 39.1% represents a substantial increase of 5.6 percentage points, primarily driven by increased revenue growth of 15% year-over-year, strategic pricing power, and a more stable supply chain environment. During our Q1 2024 earnings call, we projected an operating margin in the range of 37% to 38% for Q2 2024, so we significantly exceeded our guidance due to stronger-than-expected demand, accelerated cost savings, favorable component pricing, and, in retrospect, a somewhat conservative initial guidance.

Now to David, who will cover operational and product updates.

David Lee, Chief Technology Officer:
Thanks, Susan.

Let’s revisit wafer ASP from an innovation standpoint:
For Q2 2022, our blended wafer ASP increased by approximately 7% compared to Q1 2022 and 15% year-over-year. This favorable ASP environment reflects the persistent global semiconductor shortage, UMC's strategic investments in specialty technologies, and geographic diversification. The percentage of revenue derived from specialty technologies increased to 45% in Q2, up from 42% in Q1. The 28nm node continued to be a key revenue driver, with ASPs increasing by approximately 5% quarter-over-quarter, driven by strong demand for display driver ICs and connectivity solutions. The 40nm/55nm nodes experienced moderate ASP growth of around 3% quarter-over-quarter, with demand for power management ICs and microcontrollers remaining robust, particularly in the automotive and industrial sectors. The automotive segment witnessed the highest ASP growth among all end markets, with an increase of approximately 10% quarter-over-quarter. We anticipate that pricing will remain firm in Q3 2022, with overall wafer ASPs expected to increase by 3-5% quarter-over-quarter.

We launched NovaDrive, our new line of high-performance storage solutions, which contributed to a 12% increase in our data center segment revenue.

We’ve made strong headway with optimizing our product mix, actively collaborating with our customers to shift their product mix towards higher-margin applications and differentiated technologies. While we anticipate continued overall growth, driven by robust demand in automotive and industrial sectors, we are proactively managing short-term fluctuations in the smartphone, PC, and consumer electronics segments. We expect a modest decline in smartphone-related revenue in Q3 2024, projecting a decrease of approximately 7-9% quarter-over-quarter, but anticipate a rebound in Q4 2024. The PC segment faces continued headwinds, and we project a 5-7% decline in PC-related revenue in Q3 2024 compared to Q2 2024. The consumer electronics segment is experiencing mixed trends, and we expect a slight decrease of 2-4% in Q3 2024 compared to Q2 2024. The automotive segment continues to be a significant growth driver, and we expect a 15% increase in automotive-related revenue in Q3 2024 year-over-year, reaching $275 million. The industrial segment remains stable and continues to grow, and we anticipate a 10% increase in industrial-related revenue in Q3 2024 year-over-year. We expect meaningful results in the next few quarters, with Q3 2024 revenue expected to be in the range of $2.25 billion to $2.35 billion and gross margin to be in the range of 35% to 37%. We maintain our previous guidance of high single-digit percentage revenue growth for the full year.

Let’s move to Q&A.

Q&A SESSION

Analyst 1:
On wafer ASP, could you expand on the drivers for the projected increase in Q3?

Susan Chen:
Absolutely. We believe the continued strong demand in key sectors like automotive and industrial, coupled with ongoing capacity constraints, will support favorable pricing dynamics. Our focus on specialty technologies and long-term partnerships also contributes to our ability to command premium pricing. We are also focused on optimizing our product mix.

Analyst 2:
Regarding the product mix optimization, what's the scale and outlook?

David Lee:
We’re seeing momentum with shifting our product mix towards higher-margin applications and differentiated technologies, especially in the automotive and industrial sectors. We've secured design wins with three major smartphone clients, expecting volume production to ramp up in late Q4 and throughout 2025. We are strategically shifting our focus within the PC segment towards higher-end applications such as gaming laptops and professional workstations. We are also working with customers to diversify their consumer electronics product portfolios and leverage our specialized process technologies for innovative consumer electronics applications.

Closing

Robert Miller:
Thank you all for joining. We’re proud of our progress and excited for what’s ahead.

Operator:
Thank you. This concludes the call. You may now disconnect.
